`models` is the allowed set (None: every model); `exclude_models` drops from it. `text`
maps a payload to its representative text; a document whose text is empty stays out,
and `text_id` names the mapping so a change of representation invalidates the index
the same way a change of embedder does.

v1_live.docstring:
---
id: sldb.selfdoc.planned_document.PlannedDocument
kind: core
tags: [type:code.symbol]

---
Carry one validated documentation change and its before-image to execution.

Materializers fill ``payload`` and ``markdown`` after a render/extract
roundtrip check; ``write_documents`` persists them through SLDB tracking
and ``inspect_documents`` reads them without writing. It is a planning
record, not a filesystem transaction: ``previous`` is the before-image
captured at planning time and ``changed`` flags parser-owned drift, while
the write path re-verifies the file before saving.

v1_live.docstring: (model, diagnosis) per document that is damaged, not merely reformatted.
(model, diagnosis) per document whose text moved but whose fields held still.
Models whose roster hash disagrees although no document present is damaged.
Models whose class contract no longer matches the one the index recorded.

Whether the store is in a valid state.

A reformatted document (text moved, fields identical) is still valid, a damaged one is
not, and a disagreeing roster or root hash is not. A moved contract is not valid either:
the indexed payloads were extracted under a contract that no longer holds. Classifying
a failure is not the same as tolerating it.
